claims.text: In equiatomic high-entropy superconductors, Tc is governed primarily by lattice distortions induced by chemical disorder.
Disorder-induced lattice distortions modify electron–phonon coupling strength.
An equiatomic NbTaTiVZr-type refractory high-entropy alloy can form a fully disordered BCC state with randomly distributed constituent elements.
Annealing can induce controlled short-range order without causing phase separation.
Annealing-induced short-range order reduces random lattice distortions.
Average lattice distortion and local strain fields mediate the relationship between chemical order and electron–phonon coupling.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening and TEM strain mapping can quantify the relevant lattice distortion and local strain fields.
Chemical disorder creates significant lattice distortions.
Disorder-associated lattice distortions broaden the phonon density of states.
Disorder-associated lattice distortions modify the electron–phonon coupling constant.
Introducing short-range order partially reduces lattice distortion, changes electron–phonon coupling, and consequently shifts Tc.
Samples with increased short-range order and reduced lattice distortion will exhibit a Tc change of a few kelvin relative to as-cast, disordered samples.
The direction of the Tc shift depends on how reduced structural randomness changes electron–phonon coupling.
The as-cast alloy is fully disordered and has a characteristic Tc determined by broad phonon and electronic features.
The proposed lattice-distortion mechanism is expected to dominate when electron–phonon coupling is the primary pairing channel.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when magnetic interactions or other pairing mechanisms prevail.
The comparison is valid only when short-range order is changed without phase separation or significant secondary-phase formation.
Residual strain, annealing-induced stoichiometric variation, and other electronic correlations could affect the magnitude of the Tc shift.
If substantial, reproducible changes in chemical order and lattice distortion occur without a corresponding Tc shift, the proposed governing role of lattice distortion is falsified.
